parsed.why: Protective state: gender-identity nondiscrimination including public accommodations since 1993, hate-crime coverage, trans-panic repeal, care shield reaching visiting families, open markers, no facilities ban; only a dated 2012 custody placement. Hostile national border/entry regime still caps it.

Facilities ban in schools and state buildings with solitary-confinement prospect, no state gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage, court barred birth-certificate changes, care ban, documented state hostility to a trans organisation. Worst-legislation tier.

Most Protective tier: public-accommodations nondiscrimination since 2006, GI hate-crime, panic-defence repeal, care shield, self-attested X markers, statutorily gender-neutral restrooms; no documented local violence. Shared national border/entry regime still caps it.

Complaint-driven facilities ban whose documentary defence visitors cannot meet, flag and dorm bans, nondiscrimination omitting public accommodations. Partly offset by amendable markers and GI hate-crime coverage; still net restrictive.

Sanctuary law, comprehensive nondiscrimination, GI hate-crime, panic-defence repeal, care coverage, court-ordered restroom access. Offset by two recent trans killings in one city (raw counts, no denominator) and the shared hostile national border regime.
